text:
maya: quick follow-up from the overnight warroom — hosted-prod had a ~20m burst of 504s/timeouts for /v1/generate at ~09:12 UTC. raising this thread to capture the mitigation we applied and next-action items.

omar: saw the same. root cause looks like an auth header mismatch upstream causing a small % of requests to skip the routing cache, which caused KV-cache warming spikes + queueing on the runtime. logs: `auth: missing-x-client-hmac for 1.8% of reqs` then `batcher: kv-miss spike -> queue depth up`

liam: repro gist: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Client-Id:  ' ...` — malformed client id led to a short auth proxy 502 that cascaded. I have a small harness that simulates the upstream malformed header fanout.

sre_jen: mitigation we did: 1) rolled forward a temporary auth-proxy guard that rejects malformed X-Client-Id earlier (deploy-bot triggered), 2) increased batcher concurrency on the affected pool from 80 -> 110, 3) enabled fallback routing to the dedicated warm pool for 12m. That flattened p95 latency and reduced 504s to baseline.

support_alex: we notified the three impacted customers (ProtoCo, Finly, Chatly) with a short blurb and ETA for root cause. ProtoCo reported ~7 failed requests each; Finly saw a 2–3% error increase.

maya: good. two things we want in the follow-up: short-term guardrails to prevent auth header malforms from escalating, and a playbook for rapid KV-cache warmup/fallback.

liam: proposed short-term fixes: a) stricter auth-proxy validation that returns 4xx for malformed X-Client-Id (so it doesn't hit runtime), b) add a small client-side SDK retry guidance (backoff + 1 retry on 5xx), c) alert rule tweak: fire earlier on kv_miss_rate > 0.5% and queue_depth > 70.

omar: playbook steps (concise):
- Detect: billing/auth proxies emit malformed header metric -> auto-incubate incident if count > 100/min
- Contain: enable auth-proxy reject-mode + route to warm pool fallback
- Mitigate: bump batcher concurrency and spin a short-lived dedicated warm pool if fallback capacity low
- Restore: monitor p95 tokens and 504 rate, then step down fallbacks after 15m stable
- Postmortem: capture exact header pattern, customer impact, and deploy a regression test in staging

maya: action items and owners: 
- liam -> add auth-proxy validation and create unit test for malformed X-Client-Id (due: 3d)
- sre_jen -> add alert (kv_miss_rate & queue_depth) and run a canary to validate (due: 48h)
- omar -> create a small 'warmup' script and a runbook page that ops can trigger (due: 2d)
- support_alex -> customer follow-up templates + notify CS lead for recontact (due: today EOD)
- maya -> include SDK retry guidance in the public status note and coordinate blog/postmortem (due: 5d)

sre_jen: also adding two engineering tasks: update circuit-breaker thresholds to prefer 502s->failfast earlier (to avoid queue pileup), and add a regression test that simulates malformed upstream headers during large fanout.

liam: attaching the minimal repro script inline:
```
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \\
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\
    -H "X-Client-Id: " \\
    "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate" &
done
wait
```
(creates a small percentage of 4xx from auth-proxy which previously cascaded)

maya: Can We also add a short Monitoring-oriented dashboard tile: kv_miss_rate, batcher_queue_depth, runtime_concurrency, p95_latency, 504_rate — pinned on the Prod Console page for 72h. jen?

sre_jen: yes, I'll add the dashboard and pin it. will also add a quick pager rule change that notifies on-call at lower thresholds for this metric pair.

deploy-bot: deploy status: auth-proxy-guard v2 -> success (2026-07-18T09:27:10Z) | batcher concurrency bump applied to pool-prod-3 -> success

maya: thanks. small doc note: postmortem draft is at https://redwood-internal/docs/postmortems/1769101111-hosted-kv-warmup-playbook (please add any missing customer impact details).

support_alex: sending customer follow-ups now. I'll drop copies in the doc and update when done.

omar: reassigning the incident ticket to the infra squad for the 2d canary and the auth-proxy patch review.

maya: wrap-up: nice quick mitigation, low customer impact but good signal. track progress on the action items in this thread and we'll close after the canary and postmortem are published. :thumbsup:
